newsitem.title: USA: U.S. House tax chief sees "minor changes" in bill. [CORRECTED 20:00 GMT]
newsitem.headline: U.S. House tax chief sees "minor changes" in bill. [CORRECTED 20:00 GMT]

text.p: House Ways and Means Committee Chairman Bill Archer said Monday small changes would be made to the House tax legislation before it reaches the floor for a vote later this week.
"There will be some other minor changes," the Texas Republican said, in the House Rules Committee. But he added those changes would not "run up any big flags."

One change would be a previously announced change in the bill's child tax credit that would allow families who get a tax credit for daycare to also receive the $500 per child tax credit if their income was $50,000 or less a year.
The Rules Committee determines procedure for floor consideration of legislation, including which amendments will be allowed to be offered and the number of hours for debate.
Archer said there would be changes in Rules on terminology in the ethanol subsidy provision, but was adamant that it would still eliminate the subsidy in 2000.

Archer said differences with Senate legislation on the cigarette tax and international travel fees would be worked out later in the process when the two sides hold a conference to resolve differences and write a uniform tax bill.
The Senate bill includes a 20-cent per pack increase in the cigarette tax, which the House measure does not have.
The House bill includes a $15.50 per passenger tax for international arrivals and departures. Currently there is a $6 departure fee.
Archer said he did not support the $15.50 proposed international travel fee and that it was too big an increase. "It's certainly something that I'm going to be looking at in the conference," he said.
The Rules Committee is expected to discuss the tax legislation Tuesday (corrects from Wednesday).
